quizzes.title: Union, New States and Article 4
quizzes.passage: The opening portion of the Constitution of India is concerned with the Union and its territory. It sets out the name of the country and the basic character of its government, even though the document gives the country a federal structure. The names of the States and Union Territories, along with the extent of their territory, are listed in a schedule to the Constitution, and the number of these units has changed over time. At the time of independence in 1947, the country was made up of British Provinces and Princely States. Legislation passed in 1947 had created two separate dominions, and the Princely States were given three choices: to join India, to join Pakistan, or to remain independent. Most of the Princely States joined India, although a few refused to do so at first. Those that stayed apart were later integrated by different means. The Constitution of 1950 then classified the States and territories into four groups. The same opening provisions allow Parliament to take up new States and changes to existing ones through laws it passes. Whether such laws must follow the procedure used for constitutional amendments is answered by the Constitution itself. Over the decades, the map of India has been redrawn several times, and each change has raised questions about the boundaries and identities of the regions concerned.

questions.q: Under Article 2, admission refers to which category of States?
options: States formed by merging Union Territories
Princely States that refused to join India
questions.explanation: Admission under Article 2 refers to States already in existence, while establishment refers to States not in existence before.

questions.q: Which Article describes India, that is Bharat, as a Union of States rather than a Federation of States?
questions.explanation: Article 1 describes India, that is Bharat, as a Union of States rather than a Federation of States.

questions.q: Which schedule of the Constitution lists the names of States and Union Territories and their territorial extent?
questions.explanation: The names of States and Union Territories and their territorial extent are mentioned in the First Schedule.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Creation of a new State under Article 2 requires a constitutional amendment under Article 368.
Reason (R): Article 4 declares that laws made under Articles 2 and 3 are not amendments under Article 368.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Article 4 says such laws are not amendments under Article 368, so A is false while R is true.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Article 1   ->   C. Name of the country and type of polity
II. Article 2   ->   A. Admission or establishment of new States
III. Article 3   ->   D. Reorganisation of States, including altering boundaries and names
IV. Article 4   ->   B. Laws under Articles 2 and 3 are not amendments under Article 368
questions.explanation: Article 1 deals with the name and polity, Article 2 with admission or establishment, Article 3 with reorganisation, and Article 4 with the non-amendment rule.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Articles 1 to 4 fall under Part I of the Constitution.
II. Article 4 treats laws made under Articles 2 and 3 as amendments under Article 368.
III. The First Schedule lists the names of States and Union Territories with their territorial extent.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because Article 4 says such laws are not amendments, while I and III are correct.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Laws made under Articles 2 and 3 can be passed by a simple majority in Parliament.
II. Laws made under Articles 2 and 3 are amendments under Article 368 and need a special majority.
III. Article 1 deals with the name of the country and the type of polity.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while statement II is wrong because Article 4 says such laws are not amendments under Article 368.

Legislation passed in 1947 had created two separate dominions, and the Princely States were given three choices: to join India, to join Pakistan, or to remain independent. Most of the Princely States joined India, although a few refused to do so at first. Those that stayed apart were later integrated by different means. The Constitution of 1950 then classified the States and territories into four groups. The same opening provisions allow Parliament to take up new States and changes to existing ones through laws it passes. questions.q: Under which Part of the Constitution are the provisions on the Union and its territory placed? (Give the Part in Roman numerals.)
questions.explanation: Articles 1 to 4 fall under Part I, titled Union and its Territory.

questions.q: Under which Article is it stated that laws for admitting or establishing States are not amendments under Article 368?
questions.explanation: Article 4 declares that laws made under Articles 2 and 3 are not amendments under Article 368.

questions.q: Under Article 2, establishment refers to States that were what before the law? (Give a short phrase.)
questions.explanation: Establishment under Article 2 refers to States which were not in existence before.

questions.q: Which Article empowers Parliament to alter the boundaries of any State and change its name? (Give the number.)
questions.explanation: Article 3 empowers Parliament to reorganise States, including altering boundaries and changing names.

questions.q: Which Article sets out the amendment procedure from which laws under Articles 2 and 3 are excluded? (Give the number.)
questions.explanation: Laws under Articles 2 and 3 are not treated as amendments under Article 368.

questions.q: Which Article empowers Parliament to admit into the Union, or establish, new States? (Give the number.)
questions.explanation: Article 2 empowers Parliament to admit into the Union, or establish, new States on terms it thinks fit.

questions.q: Which Article deals with the name of the country and the type of polity? (Give the number.)
questions.explanation: Article 1 deals with the name of the country and the type of polity.

quizzes.title: Commissions on Linguistic States
quizzes.passage: Demands for States organised on linguistic lines grew in several parts of the country after independence, and the government responded by setting up bodies to examine the question. Each of them examined the linguistic factor, but they did not reach the same conclusions. The creation of one State on a linguistic basis intensified demands from other regions, which pushed the government to take up the whole question again. Reorganisation was therefore examined more than once before a final framework was adopted. The change was made through a law passed by Parliament and a constitutional amendment passed in the same year. Together these measures shaped the map of India as it stood after that year. The original Constitution divided the States and Territories into four categories. A three-member commission was appointed to re-examine the whole question, and its suggestions included abolishing those categories. Under the Constitution, Parliament holds the power to reorganise States, which can involve forming a new State by separating territory, merging States, altering boundaries, or changing the name of a State. Later changes, such as the renaming of Orissa as Odisha, show that the same power has continued to be used. The bodies examined the linguistic question at different points in time.

questions.q: In which month and year was the Linguistic Provinces Commission under SK Dhar appointed?
questions.explanation: The Dhar Commission was appointed in June 1948 to examine reorganisation on the linguistic factor.

questions.q: Which theory of State reorganisation did the Fazl Ali Commission reject, even though it broadly accepted language as the basis?
questions.explanation: The Fazl Ali Commission rejected the theory of One Language - One State.

questions.q: In which month and year was the Fazl Ali Commission appointed to re-examine the question?
questions.explanation: The Fazl Ali Commission was appointed in December 1953 to re-examine the whole question.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Andhra State was created by separating Telugu-speaking areas from Madras State.
Reason (R): The creation of Andhra State intensified demand from other regions for States on a linguistic basis.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but R describes the effect of the creation of Andhra and does not explain how it was created.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Dhar Commission   ->   C. Administrative convenience over the linguistic factor
II. JVP Committee   ->   A. Formally rejected language as the basis of reorganisation
III. Fazl Ali Commission   ->   D. Broadly accepted language but rejected One Language - One State
IV. States Reorganisation Act, 1956   ->   B. Created 14 States and 6 Union Territories
questions.explanation: The Dhar Commission recommended administrative convenience, the JVP Committee rejected language, the Fazl Ali Commission accepted language broadly, and the 1956 Act created 14 States and 6 UTs.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The JVP Committee submitted its report in April 1949.
II. The JVP Committee formally accepted language as the basis for reorganisation of States.
III. The States Reorganisation Act and a constitutional amendment created 14 States and 6 Union Territories on 1 November 1956.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the JVP Committee rejected language as the basis, while I and III are correct.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The Fazl Ali Commission submitted its report in 1953.
II. The Fazl Ali Commission was a body of three members.
III. The Fazl Ali Commission suggested abolishing the four-fold classification of States.
questions.explanation: Statements II and III are correct, while statement I is wrong because the report was submitted in September 1955.

questions.q: In which month and year did the Fazl Ali Commission submit its report? (Give the month and year.)
questions.explanation: The Fazl Ali Commission submitted its report in September 1955.

questions.q: Which theory of State reorganisation did the Fazl Ali Commission reject? (Give a short phrase.)
questions.explanation: The Fazl Ali Commission broadly accepted language as the basis but rejected One Language - One State.

questions.q: On which date were 14 States and 6 Union Territories created on 1 November 1956 under the States Reorganisation Act and a related amendment? (Give the date.)
questions.explanation: The States Reorganisation Act and a related amendment created 14 States and 6 Union Territories on 1 November 1956.

questions.q: In which year was Andhra State created by separating Telugu-speaking areas from Madras State? (Give the year.)
questions.explanation: Andhra State was created in 1953 by separating Telugu-speaking areas from Madras State.

questions.q: In which month and year was the Linguistic Provinces Commission under SK Dhar appointed? (Give the month and year.)
questions.explanation: The Dhar Commission was appointed in June 1948 under the chairmanship of SK Dhar.

questions.q: In which month and year did the JVP Committee submit its report? (Give the month and year.)
questions.explanation: The JVP Committee submitted its report in April 1949.

questions.q: In which month and year did the Dhar Commission submit its report? (Give the month and year.)
questions.explanation: The Dhar Commission submitted its report in December 1948.
